hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap as needs outpace available money
hero.teaser: Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall, and the gap between what the county needs and what it can afford could shape how residents get around for decades.
hero.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next 20 years, a gap that could determine how residents travel for decades to come.

The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements through 2050, but only $701 million is currently available. That means the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Nearly all of the available funding comes from state and federal sources, with only $10 million coming from local revenue. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August and outlines transportation needs across roads, transit, aviation, freight, and other infrastructure categories.

Among the most pressing unfunded needs are nine roads the county identified as requiring widening as traffic grows. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, money that is not currently available, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. Without funding for these widening projects, the county will be unable to address growing congestion on these corridors.

State Road 710 stands out as among the county's highest priorities and has been the subject of repeated safety concerns. About $300 million in projects are planned for the corridor, reflecting the urgent need for improvements on this route. The massive funding shortfall highlights the challenge facing Martin County as it tries to balance transportation demands with limited financial resources over the coming decades.

cards.headline: Florida voter data highlighted in declassified intelligence reports as Trump renews election security push
cards.body:
President Donald Trump renewed debate over election security during his Thursday national address, while newly released intelligence records put a spotlight on publicly available Florida voter-registration data. Trump urged Congress to adopt tighter voting restrictions and repeated unsubstantiated claims about the 2020 election, declaring that mail-in ballots are inherently corrupt.

One declassified report says a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter-registration information from commercial websites in 2022. The same actor also obtained records from Colorado, Connecticut, Michigan, Oklahoma and Rhode Island. Another intelligence record lists Florida among 18 states whose voter information was obtained for possible identity matching and public-opinion analysis. The records describe the collection of voter information, some of it publicly available, but do not say Florida ballots or vote totals were altered. The 2022 report also says the actor's motive was unknown.

The White House characterized the broader collection effort as a major compromise of American voter data. An earlier federal assessment of the 2022 elections found no evidence that detected foreign cyber activity prevented voting, changed votes or compromised the integrity of ballots. Trump did not single out Florida in his address, but the declassified records released by his White House did reference the state.

The week also brought major courtroom developments for two Florida state lawmakers. Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon learned she will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Nixon and other protesters occupied the area for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave. Nixon calls the prosecution political and has incorporated the case into her campaign for U.S. Senate, where she is challenging retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman for the Democratic nomination in Florida's Aug. 18 primary. Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe ended the week facing a $450,000 civil judgment after a Leon County jury found him liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation. The case was brought by former legislative aide Nicolas Frevola, former intern Jacob Cutbirth and Frevola's mother. Basabe represented himself despite having no legal training and continues to deny the underlying allegations.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September due to low demand
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. The decision reflects how the airline industry operates based on demand.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot at success. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He emphasized the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying "It's easy. It's close." Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time.

Dambeck said the Boston route is performing well and seeing great demand. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. Regarding JetBlue's ridership on the JFK route, he said the airline was "just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for." Despite the cancellation, Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route returning in the future. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.

cards.headline: Jury orders Florida Rep. Fabian Basabe to pay $450,000 in sexual harassment, battery case
cards.teaser: A Leon County jury found Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation, ordering him to pay $450,000 to former legislative aide Nicolas Frevola, former intern Jacob Cutbirth and Frevola's mother.
cards.body:
Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe ended the week facing a $450,000 civil judgment after a Leon County jury found him liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation. The case was brought by former legislative aide Nicolas Frevola, former intern Jacob Cutbirth and Frevola's mother. Basabe represented himself despite having no legal training. The trial was repeatedly interrupted by procedural mistakes and violations of the judge's orders. Circuit Judge J. Lee Marsh told him that if an attorney had done half of what he had done, they would have been sanctioned. Basabe told jurors he represented himself because he wanted to demonstrate that he had nothing to hide. After the verdict, however, he acknowledged that proceeding without an attorney was a mistake.

Basabe continues to deny the underlying allegations. He has not been criminally charged, and an outside ethics investigation conducted for the Florida House previously reached an inconclusive finding. His political opponents quickly called for his resignation. Basabe is seeking reelection this fall, and the verdict could also renew questions about whether House leaders will pursue disciplinary action.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth backs Blue Angels low-altitude Pensacola beach flyover as safety scrutiny mounts
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is encouraging low-altitude military flyovers after a Blue Angels fighter jet buzzed a crowded Pensacola beach Wednesday, flying so low that chairs and tents went flying and sand kicked up.
cards.body:
Video spreading widely on social media shows a jet from the Navy's Blue Angels demonstration squadron flying so low over a crowded Pensacola beach on Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears. The U.S. Navy said in a statement shortly afterward that it was conducting a thorough safety review. Then on Thursday morning, Trump administration officials heaped praise on the maneuver. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote on his personal X account that the flyovers will continue until morale improves. The Pentagon's top spokesman, Sean Parnell, wrote Carry on Patriots on social media alongside a photo showing a Blue Angels jet with a wingtip just feet above the heads of beachgoers.

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said the Navy had no problem with the flight and there would be no reprimands or firings. His social media post was retweeted by Hegseth. Cao's post said Thursday that the Blue Angels conducted a flight debrief. Navy officials would not say if that debrief, typically a routine occurrence after every flight, was the thorough safety review the Navy said it would conduct the day prior. Aviation safety consultant Jeff Guzzetti, who used to investigate crashes for both the National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration, said it is shocking that the top leaders of the military would excuse this type of reckless behavior. A cavalier attitude like that can only lead to accidents in my view, he said.

cards.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast seeks fosters and adopters during shelter renovation
cards.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation.
cards.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation. The construction will modernize the shelter, improve animal living spaces, enhance adoption areas, and create more comfortable and visible spaces to care for animals. The renovation presents significant challenges for the animals, who are being held in smaller spaces during the work.

"These animals are really being affected by the sound of the construction," Sarah Fisher of the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast said. "It's very, very loud and as you can imagine the sound being in a closed kennel can be very stressful for an animal." About 50 animals are currently in foster care, but the shelter is hoping to get the remaining 67 animals housed on-site either fostered or adopted, with most of them being dogs. The shelter continues to receive animals daily and is on a mission to get them out as quickly as they come in.

hero.headline: MLB restricts dugout iPad use to prevent artificial intelligence from making game decisions
hero.teaser: Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible starting Wednesday night to prevent teams from using artificial intelligence to help make in-game decisions.
hero.body:
Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night when the second half of the season started. The league took the action to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs.

MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches. A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Argentina rallies past England 2-1 to reach World Cup final
cards.teaser: Argentina scored two late goals to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinals and advance to Sunday's final against Spain.
cards.body:
Argentina overcame a 1-0 deficit with two goals in the final minutes to defeat England 2-1 on Wednesday and advance to the World Cup final. Enzo Fernandez scored the equalizer in the 85th minute, and substitute Lautaro Martinez headed in the winner two minutes into stoppage time after receiving a cross from Lionel Messi.

England had taken the lead in the 55th minute when Anthony Gordon scored. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves and Alexis Mac Allister sent a header off the post as Argentina pressed for the equalizer. At the final whistle, Messi fell to his knees in celebration while England players collapsed in disbelief.

The defending champions will face Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team proved its collectiveness and brotherhood by fighting to the very end. England captain Harry Kane said the team was gutted after giving every bit of blood, sweat and tears to reach the semifinals.

cards.headline: Security ramped up for World Cup final with Trump attending trophy presentation
cards.teaser: Federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies are implementing a security plan two years in the making for Sunday's World Cup final in New Jersey, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation.
cards.body:
A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. For Sunday's match, FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there is anything that needs to be done from a threat perspective.

The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security.

cards.headline: Spain advances to World Cup final with victory over France
cards.teaser: Spain defeated France 2-0 to advance to the World Cup final, where they will face Argentina on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
cards.body:
Argentina rallied from a 1-0 deficit to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinals on Wednesday, with goals from Enzo Fernandez in the 85th minute and substitute Lautaro Martinez in stoppage time. England captain Harry Kane's team had taken the lead through Anthony Gordon's goal in the 55th minute, but Argentina's comeback kept the defending champions' hopes of back-to-back titles alive. Martinez said he had told teammate Alexis Mac Allister before the match that he would come on and win it. At the final whistle, 39-year-old Lionel Messi fell to his knees in celebration while England players collapsed in disbelief. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves and Mac Allister sent a header off the post as Argentina pressed for the equalizer.

Argentina will face European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said his team will try to win and leave everything out there, adding that the team is unique and that statement comes from the heart, not arrogance. Messi, likely playing at his last World Cup, is one win away from further strengthening his case to be considered the greatest soccer player of all time. For England, the loss marks the third time they have fallen short in World Cup semifinals after losses to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018.

cards.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts qualify for Junior Olympics with top 15 national finish
cards.body:
Three young gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer qualified for the Junior Olympics after securing a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine came to gymnastics through different paths but now compete as one unit on the national stage. Rose-Daris said it wasn't really about gymnastics at first but the fact that she knew how to do a cartwheel. Supan was inspired by the gymnasts she saw on YouTube and how amazing they are and how fun it looks. Rine said she loves it because she learns new things.

Head Coach Candice Lazuka described the season as strong, with the team competing locally, traveling, and advancing through states and regionals. At AAU Nationals, the gymnasts scored a 9.9, coming very close to a perfect 10. Lazuka said it's hard to get a perfect 10, but they came very close. The finish qualified the team for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Rose-Daris said it's going to be really fun that she's going to an entire different part of the world. Supan said the experience is happy and exciting at the same time. Rine shared her focus heading into the Junior Olympics: getting first place on floors.

cards.headline: Alex Vindman raises $8.5 million for Florida Senate race, expanding fundraising lead
cards.teaser: Retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman tightened his grip on the Democratic money lead during the second quarter, raising $8.5 million and pushing his total receipts above $16 million in the race for Florida's U.S. Senate seat.
cards.body:
Vindman tightened his grip on the Democratic money lead during the second quarter, raising $8.5 million and pushing his total receipts above $16 million. He said Republicans woke up with a bit of a panic, stating there is no denying that the Florida Senate race is in play. Republican Sen. Ashley Moody reported raising another $3.6 million. Her campaign also promoted polling showing her leading either Vindman or Nixon in a potential general-election matchup.

Moody was appointed to the Senate after Marco Rubio resigned to become secretary of state. The November special election will determine who serves the final two years of Rubio's term. Vindman is challenging Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon in the Aug. 18 primary. She and other protesters occupied the area for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave. cards.headline: Florida gubernatorial candidate James Fishback faces residency challenge in court
cards.teaser: Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback will defend his eligibility to remain in the primary as opponent Lt. Jay Collins argues that records showing Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., mean he does not satisfy Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governor.
cards.body:
Lt. Jay Collins, one of Fishback's opponents in the Republican gubernatorial primary, argues that records showing Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., mean he does not satisfy Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governor. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida and maintained the state as his permanent home. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin Tuesday in Tallahassee.

Because primary ballots have already been printed, the judge has said a ruling against Fishback could require election officials to post notices and decline to count votes cast for him. The case represents another looming legal fight over the Republican primary for governor.

cards.headline: Florida Rep. Angie Nixon to stand trial in September on charges stemming from Capitol sit-in
cards.teaser: Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office, where she and other protesters objected to Florida's newly approved congressional map.
cards.body:

Nixon and other protesters occupied the area for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map, which could help Republicans add up to four seats in the U.S. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave. Nixon said following Wednesday's hearing that if they think the threat of a trial is going to make her back down, they picked the wrong woman. Ashley Moody reported raising another $3.6 million.

cards.headline: Pensacola beachgoer calls Blue Angels low flyover 'once-in-a-lifetime experience' as military reviews safety
cards.teaser: Florida beachgoer Alexandra Belcher called the Blue Angels flyover a once-in-a-lifetime experience, saying she didn't realize how close the jet was until everyone around her reacted.
cards.body:
Florida beachgoer Alexandra Belcher, 34, called the Blue Angels flyover this week a once-in-a-lifetime experience. She said she didn't realize how close it was until everyone around her remarked how cool it was. Belcher said it was not normal, but it was such a blessing to be able to witness that with everybody that she was with. The reaction contrasts with safety concerns raised by aviation experts about the Wednesday maneuver in Pensacola, where a Blue Angels jet flew so low over a crowded beach that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears.

Former Transportation Department Inspector General Mary Schiavo said these flyovers probably don't violate military rules because the Pentagon doesn't have the same restrictions on flying low over people that the FAA imposes on civilian flights. But that doesn't mean they are a good idea, particularly the risky maneuvers that Blue Angels pilots perform. Schiavo, who is also a pilot and used to work in air shows years ago, said what the Blue Angels do is exceedingly dangerous, amazing and wonderful, but dangerous, and so it is really not something to be performed over people. Aviation safety consultant Jeff Guzzetti, who used to investigate crashes for both the National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration, called the behavior reckless.

cards.headline: FDOT to Hold Public Workshops on Willoughby Boulevard Improvement Study
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Transportation will hold two public workshops to discuss proposed improvements along Willoughby Boulevard between Monterey Road and U.S. 1 in Martin Count
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Transportation will hold two public workshops to discuss proposed improvements along Willoughby Boulevard between Monterey Road and U.S. 1 in Martin County.

The meetings are part of a Project Development and Environment, or PD&E, study examining potential alternatives for the corridor. FDOT will offer the workshop in virtual and in-person formats, and each meeting will include a presentation followed by an opportunity for residents to ask questions and provide feedback.

## Virtual workshop scheduled for July 28

The virtual workshop will begin at **5:30 p.m. Tuesday, July 28.** Participants must register in advance at [https://tinyurl.com/Willoughby-APW](https://tinyurl.com/Willoughby-APW).

People who prefer to join by phone can call **1-469-423-0557** and enter access code 35124623#.

Registered participants will receive an email containing a link to join the meeting. Those attending from a mobile device will need the free Microsoft Teams application. FDOT recommends allowing enough time to log in before the presentation begins.

## In-person workshop scheduled for July 29

The in-person workshop will begin at **5:30 p.m. Wednesday, July 29,** at the 10th Street Community Center, 724 SE 10th Street, Stuart, FL 34994.

The meeting will use an open-house format. FDOT staff will be available to explain the proposed alternatives, answer questions and assist attendees.

Questions and comments will be addressed in the order they are received. If a question cannot be answered during the event, FDOT will provide a written response after the meeting. Residents may also submit questions or comments before the workshop by contacting the project manager.

## What the study will evaluate

A PD&E study is an early phase of the transportation planning process used to evaluate possible improvements and determine how a project could move forward.

The process typically considers traffic operations, roadway safety, environmental effects, community impacts, engineering needs and estimated costs. Feedback gathered during the workshops will help FDOT evaluate the proposed alternatives for Willoughby Boulevard.

## Accessibility accommodations available

Anyone requiring accommodations under the Americans with Disabilities Act should contact FDOT at least seven days before the meeting.

Accommodation requests may be directed to FDOT Project Manager Vanita Saini, P.E., at **954-777-4468** or [Vanita.Saini@dot.state.fl.us](mailto:Vanita.Saini@dot.state.fl.us). Written requests may be mailed to the Florida Department of Transportation, 3400 West Commercial Boulevard, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33309.

People with hearing or speech impairments may contact the Florida Relay Service at 1-800-955-8771 for TDD service or 1-800-955-8770 for voice service.

For additional project information, contact Saini at 954-777-4468 or toll-free at 866-336-8435, extension 4468.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce woman wins $5 million on $20 scratch-off ticket
hero.body:
Florida Lottery officials announced Friday that Maria Duran, 57, of St. Lucie County claimed a $5 million top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6. Duran chose to receive her winnings as a one-time, lump-sum payment of $3,262,138.

hero.headline: JetBlue ending Vero Beach to JFK route in September due to low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He explained that JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said. However, not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He emphasized the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said.

Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time. Dambeck said that route is performing well and noted that Boston is seeing great demand. As for whether the JFK route could return in the future, Dambeck said the door is not closed. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major I-95 Ramp Closures Planned July 19-24
hero.teaser:
Motorists across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 17-24 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department
hero.body:
Motorists across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 17-24 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report highlights multiple full road and ramp closures expected to have the greatest impact on drivers.

## Major closures to know about

### Southbound I-95 exit to Bridge Road closing overnight

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, also known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

Motorists will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt-Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road.

The closure is needed for roadway construction. FDOT has scheduled July 26-30 as contingency dates in case the work is delayed by weather or other unforeseen conditions.

### Martin Highway ramps closing at I-95

Two ramps serving Martin Highway at I-95 will close overnight from **Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to Martin Highway at Exit 110 will be closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Drivers will continue north to Becker Road at Exit 114, travel west on Becker Road and use southbound I-95 to return to the Martin Highway exit.

The northbound I-95 entrance ramp from Martin Highway will also be closed during the same hours. Motorists will be detoured east on Martin Highway, north on Newfield Parkway and west on Becker Road to reach the northbound I-95 entrance ramp.

FDOT said only one ramp closure will occur at a time.

### Orange Avenue exit closing in Fort Pierce

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

Drivers will be detoured to the eastbound Orange Avenue exit, north on Jenkins Road and west on Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue.

The work includes paving and lighting installation. Contingency dates are scheduled for July 26-30.

### Emergency repairs could cause major delays on I-95

Southbound I-95 between Kanner Highway and Bridge Road will have **two lanes closed beginning at 4 p.m. Monday, July 20, and Tuesday, July 21.** The lanes are scheduled to reopen by 5:30 a.m. each morning.

FDOT said the closures are needed to complete an emergency repair near mile marker 98. Drivers are encouraged to consider alternate routes because the early closure time could affect the evening commute.

### Port St. Lucie neighborhood roads may close for several days

Extended closures are planned along several roads near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project. Closures may begin at **7 a.m. Monday, July 20, and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, July 24,** on portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue.

The roads will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. Adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained throughout the work.

Detours will use nearby roads including SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and SW McDevitt Avenue. FDOT is also providing advance notice that SW Paar Drive between SW McIntosh Street and SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard may close from July 27-31.

## Martin County traffic impacts

Northbound and southbound I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line will continue to have two lanes closed overnight for milling, resurfacing and signage work.

U.S. 1 between Fischer Street and Decker Avenue may have two lanes closed intermittently from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday for sign installation.

A1A between Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced to one lane at times Monday through Friday for pavement widening and drainage work. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic through the work zone.

Martin Highway between Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard may have intermittent overnight lane closures Tuesday through Thursday for milling and resurfacing.

In Stuart, two westbound lanes on Monterey Road between Ocean Boulevard and Monterey Commons Boulevard may close from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. Tuesday through Thursday.

## St. Lucie County traffic impacts

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road may have daytime lane closures Monday through Friday. Two lanes may close overnight from Sunday through Friday for drainage work, milling and repaving.

U.S. 1 between Jennings Road and Golden Oak Trail may also have lane restrictions during daytime and overnight hours.

SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Jordin Avenue and Alcantarra Boulevard will have intermittent lane closures from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday.

Up to two lanes may close overnight on I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and the area just south of Okeechobee Road for milling and repaving.

Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road will continue to have intermittent weekday lane closures as part of the widening project.

## North Causeway marine restrictions continue

Boaters traveling near the North Causeway Bridge in Fort Pierce could encounter partial or full channel closures as crews continue removing sections of the former drawbridge.

Partial channel restrictions may occur during daylight hours on weekdays through late 2026. At least 45 feet of the channel is expected to remain open during partial closures.

Intermittent full channel closures lasting up to six hours may occur through July for the removal of steel bascule bridge spans. Vessels requiring full channel access must provide the bridge tender with 120 minutes of advance notice.

The new North Causeway Bridge remains open to vehicle traffic, although nearby roads including U.S. 1, Old Dixie Highway, Juanita Avenue and Harbortown Drive may have lane restrictions.

## Indian River County traffic impacts

One lane may remain closed on the 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive as bridge rehabilitation continues.

I-95 near the new Oslo Road interchange may have one or two lanes closed overnight Sunday through Thursday for bridge work, milling and resurfacing.

On 90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, one lane may close overnight Sunday through Friday for roadway construction.

Drivers near Sebastian Inlet should expect intermittent lane and shoulder closures on A1A from July 20-31. Flaggers will direct traffic through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park remain closed during construction of the replacement bridge, although the park, boat ramp and portions of both parking areas remain open.

## Additional I-95 closures coming the following week

FDOT is also providing advance notice of several closures scheduled to begin Sunday, July 26. All four I-95 ramps at Midway Road are expected to close separately overnight through July 31 for paving. Only one ramp will close at a time.

Detours will use St. Lucie West Boulevard, U.S. 1 and nearby interstate exits. Additional ramp closures are also planned later at Martin Highway and Kanner Highway.

Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Drivers should allow additional travel time, follow posted detours and use caution around workers and equipment.

Real-time interstate traffic conditions are available through [Florida 511](https://fl511.com). Updated lane closure information is available through [FDOT District Four](https://www.fdot.gov/info/co/district4).
